questions.question: What is the most common viral agent of acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Coxsackie virus B, an enterovirus, is the most common viral cause of acute myocarditis in developed countries, especially in young adults.

questions.question: What major pathophysiological mechanism damages cardiomyocytes in Coxsackie B myocarditis?
questions.explanation: The initial damage is by direct cytolysis of the Coxsackie B virus, followed by an immune response that amplifies the myocardial injury.

questions.question: What is the most common clinical presentation in a patient with Coxsackie B myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Chest pain, often pleuritic or anginal, together with dyspnea and fatigue, constitutes the typical clinical picture of acute viral myocarditis.

questions.question: What is the confirmatory diagnosis in acute Coxsackie B myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Endomyocardial biopsy is the gold standard to confirm myocarditis, showing inflammatory infiltrate and myocyte necrosis.

questions.question: What initial treatment is recommended in acute Coxsackie B myocarditis with ventricular dysfunction?
questions.explanation: Initial management focuses on the treatment of heart failure (ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, diuretics), since there is no specific approved antiviral therapy.

questions.question: Which electrocardiographic finding is typical in acute Coxsackie B myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Diffuse ST-segment elevation, often without pathologic Q waves, is the characteristic electrocardiographic finding of acute viral myocarditis.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of acute myocarditis in developed countries?
questions.explanation: Acute myocarditis in developed countries is mainly caused by viral infections, notably parvovirus B19 and human herpes virus 6, which cause direct myocardial damage or by immune response.

questions.question: Which electrocardiographic finding is characteristic of acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Diffuse ST segment elevation, without mirror image, is typical of acute myocarditis and distinguishes it from ST elevation infarction, where the elevation is regional and with reciprocal changes.

questions.question: Which biomarker is typically elevated in acute myocarditis with myocardial damage?
questions.explanation: Troponin I is elevated in acute myocarditis due to myocyte necrosis, although its elevation is lower than in infarction; Its sensitivity is high but specificity is limited, supporting the diagnosis along with clinical and imaging.

questions.question: What is the first-line treatment in acute myocarditis with ventricular dysfunction?
questions.explanation: In acute myocarditis with ventricular dysfunction, heart failure treatment is used, including ACEI or ARB, beta blockers and diuretics; Corticosteroids are reserved for autoimmune causes or giant cell myocarditis.

questions.question: What imaging test confirms the diagnosis of acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is the non-invasive technique of choice to confirm myocarditis, showing myocardial edema, hyperemia and fibrosis or necrosis with the Lake Louise criteria, being superior to other modalities.

questions.question: Which symptom of the classic triad indicates the worst prognosis in acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Heart failure in acute myocarditis reflects significant ventricular dysfunction and is associated with greater mortality and the need for transplantation, unlike chest pain or fever, which usually indicate a more benign presentation.

questions.question: What electrocardiographic pattern is characteristic of acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Acute myocarditis classically presents diffuse ST-segment elevation and PR depression, reflecting global myocardial damage rather than a single coronary territory.

questions.question: En el ECG de un paciente con miocarditis aguda, ¿qué otro hallazgo suele acompañar a la elevación difusa del ST?
questions.explanation: PR depression is a distinctive finding of acute pericarditis and myocarditis, secondary to atrial inflammation, and usually accompanies diffuse ST elevation.

questions.question: Which of the following electrocardiographic findings is more typical of acute myocarditis than of acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction?
questions.explanation: Diffuse ST elevation without coronary distribution is characteristic of myocarditis, while infarction usually shows localized elevation in a specific territory.

questions.question: What pathophysiological mechanism explains diffuse ST elevation in acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Diffuse inflammation of the myocardium causes global damage that alters repolarization in all leads, producing diffuse ST elevation and PR depression.

questions.question: En un paciente con miocarditis aguda, ¿cuál es el tratamiento de primera línea cuando hay elevación difusa del ST y depresión del PR?
questions.explanation: El tratamiento inicial de la miocarditis aguda se centra en el soporte y el manejo de la insuficiencia cardíaca, no en antiinflamatorios de rutina que pueden aumentar el daño miocárdico.

questions.question: ¿Qué hallazgo de laboratorio es más útil para apoyar el diagnóstico de miocarditis aguda en presencia de elevación difusa del ST?
questions.explanation: Elevation of troponin indicates myocardial damage, but in myocarditis it does not follow the typical pattern of infarction; Its elevation together with the diffuse ECG supports the diagnosis.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of acute myocarditis with elevated troponin and normal coronary arteries?
questions.explanation: Acute myocarditis is usually of viral etiology, especially due to parvovirus B19 and Epstein-Barr virus, which explains the elevation of troponin with angiographically normal coronary arteries.

questions.question: Which cardiac magnetic resonance finding is characteristic of acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Late gadolinium enhancement in myocarditis is usually epicardial or intramyocardial, unlike the subendocardial or transmural pattern typical of infarction, which helps differentiate both entities.

questions.question: ¿Qué tratamiento está indicado en miocarditis aguda con disfunción ventricular?
questions.explanation: En miocarditis con disfunción ventricular se instaura tratamiento de insuficiencia cardiaca con IECA o ARA II y betabloqueantes; los corticoides solo se reservan para causas autoinmunes o específicas.

questions.question: ¿Qué dato clínico apoya el diagnóstico de miocarditis en paciente con troponina elevada?
questions.explanation: Acute myocarditis usually presents with chest pain, dyspnea, and signs of heart failure; Fever and arthralgia are less specific and point to other systemic etiologies.

questions.question: What is the most feared complication in the acute phase of myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Ventricular arrhythmias, including ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation, are the main cause of sudden death in the acute phase of myocarditis, especially in patients with ventricular dysfunction.

questions.question: What test confirms normal coronary arteries in suspected myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Coronary angiography is the standard for ruling out obstructive coronary disease, allowing troponin elevation to be attributed to myocarditis when there is compatible clinical and imaging evidence.

questions.question: What is the gold standard for the definitive diagnosis of acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Endomyocardial biopsy is the reference procedure to confirm myocarditis, allowing histological and immunohistochemical analysis. MRI is useful but not definitive, and the other options evaluate other causes.

questions.question: What clinical criterion justifies performing endomyocardial biopsy in suspected myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Endomyocardial biopsy is indicated in acute myocarditis when there is recent onset ventricular dysfunction, especially with hemodynamic instability or severe arrhythmias. Fever, atypical pain or isolated palpitations are not indications.

questions.question: What histological finding confirms giant cell myocarditis?
questions.explanation: La miocarditis por células gigantes se caracteriza por necrosis miocárdica con infiltrado inflamatorio y células gigantes multinucleadas. Es una causa rara pero agresiva, y su identificación en la biopsia es crucial por su mal pronóstico.

questions.question: ¿Qué tinción se utiliza para detectar infiltrado inflamatorio en biopsia endomiocárdica?
questions.explanation: La hematoxilina-eosina es la tinción estándar para evaluar infiltrados inflamatorios en la biopsia endomiocárdica. Las otras tinciones son específicas para bacterias, micobacterias y parásitos, no para el diagnóstico de miocarditis.

questions.question: ¿Qué complicación se asocia con mayor frecuencia a la biopsia endomiocárdica?
questions.explanation: La perforación cardíaca es la complicación más temida de la biopsia endomiocárdica, pudiendo causar taponamiento. Aunque es poco frecuente, el riesgo es mayor en centros con baja experiencia o en pacientes con miocarditis aguda.

questions.question: How many endomyocardial biopsy samples are recommended for diagnosis of myocarditis?
questions.explanation: At least 5 to 6 endomyocardial biopsy samples are recommended to increase the diagnostic sensitivity of myocarditis, due to the patchy distribution of the inflammatory infiltrate.

questions.question: What histological finding defines the Dallas criteria for active myocarditis?
options: Amyloid deposition in the myocardial interstitium
questions.explanation: The Dallas criterion for active myocarditis requires necrosis or myocyte degeneration associated with interstitial inflammatory infiltrate, excluding typical ischemic changes.

questions.question: What is the Dallas subtype of myocarditis that shows inflammation without necrosis?
questions.explanation: Borderline myocarditis according to the Dallas criteria presents inflammatory infiltrate without necrosis or myocyte degeneration, differentiating it from the active form that does include cellular damage.

questions.question: ¿Qué tinción es esencial para confirmar infiltrado inflamatorio en biopsia endomiocárdica?
questions.explanation: La hematoxilina-eosina es la tinción estándar para evaluar infiltrados inflamatorios y necrosis en la biopsia endomiocárdica, siendo fundamental en la aplicación de los criterios de Dallas.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es la principal limitación de los criterios de Dallas en la práctica clínica?
questions.explanation: Los criterios de Dallas tienen una concordancia interobservador limitada (kappa baja) y sensibilidad reducida por el muestreo, lo que ha llevado a complementarlos con inmunohistoquímica y PCR viral.

questions.question: What number of endomyocardial biopsies is recommended to increase diagnostic sensitivity?
questions.explanation: Se recomienda obtener al menos 5 biopsias de diferentes regiones del ventrículo derecho para reducir el error de muestreo, ya que la inflamación miocárdica suele ser parcheada.

questions.question: ¿En qué contexto clínico está indicada la biopsia endomiocárdica según criterios actuales?
options: Dolor torácico típico con troponina normal
questions.explanation: La biopsia endomiocárdica está indicada en miocarditis fulminante o con arritmias malignas, cuando el diagnóstico etiológico puede cambiar el manejo, no en cuadros leves o autolimitados.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es la causa más frecuente de miocarditis aguda en jóvenes previamente sanos?
questions.explanation: In young people, acute myocarditis is classically secondary to viral infections, especially enterovirus, parvovirus B19, and Epstein-Barr virus. Other etiologies such as autoimmune or toxic are less prevalent in this group.

questions.question: Which virus is most frequently associated with fulminant myocarditis in young adults?
questions.explanation: Parvovirus B19 is the most commonly identified viral agent in acute and fulminant myocarditis in young adults, although others such as human herpesvirus 6 are also implicated. The correct answer reflects current epidemiology.

questions.question: What is the most common initial symptom in a young person with acute viral myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Chest pain is the most common presenting symptom in young people with viral myocarditis, simulating an acute coronary syndrome. Other symptoms such as dyspnea or syncope are less frequent at the beginning.

questions.question: Which electrocardiographic finding is most characteristic in acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Diffuse ST segment elevation without mirror image is typical of acute myocarditis, unlike infarction where it is regional. Other findings such as Q waves or blocks appear in advanced stages or complications.

questions.question: What is the first-line treatment in uncomplicated acute viral myocarditis?
questions.explanation: In uncomplicated acute viral myocarditis, treatment is supportive, including rest, management of heart failure, and antiarrhythmics if necessary. Immunosuppression is not routinely indicated without evidence of an autoimmune cause.

questions.question: ¿Qué prueba de imagen es la más sensible para confirmar miocarditis aguda no invasiva?
questions.explanation: La resonancia magnética cardiaca con realce tardío de gadolinio es la técnica no invasiva más sensible para detectar miocarditis, mostrando edema y fibrosis miocárdica. Otras imágenes son menos específicas o invasivas.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es el hallazgo ecocardiográfico más característico en la miocarditis aguda con disfunción ventricular?
questions.explanation: En la miocarditis aguda, la disfunción ventricular suele manifestarse como hipocinesia global o segmentaria, aunque también puede haber dilatación; la hipertrofia concéntrica y la hiperdinamia no son típicas.

questions.question: What echocardiographic finding suggests pericardial involvement in acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Pericardial effusion is the direct echocardiographic manifestation of the accompanying pericardial inflammation in myocarditis, while the other options correspond to unrelated valvular or aortic pathologies.

questions.question: Which echocardiographic parameter best evaluates left ventricular systolic function in acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Left ventricular ejection fraction is the standard index to quantify global systolic function; The other parameters assess diameters, hypertrophy or diastolic function, not global contractility.

questions.question: What is a serious echocardiographic complication that may be seen in acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Cardiac tamponade may occur when pericardial effusion associated with myocarditis accumulates rapidly, compromising diastolic filling; the other options are chronic or unrelated entities.

questions.question: In acute myocarditis, which echocardiographic pattern of ventricular dysfunction is most common?
questions.explanation: La disfunción en miocarditis suele ser segmentaria o global, pero no sigue un territorio coronario; el patrón isquémico es más típico de enfermedad coronaria, mientras que los otros patrones corresponden a otras miocardiopatías.

questions.question: ¿Qué hallazgo en el ecocardiograma indica mayor gravedad en un paciente con miocarditis aguda?
questions.explanation: Una fracción de eyección notablemente reducida (30%) junto con derrame pericárdico severo refleja disfunción ventricular importante y compromiso pericárdico extenso, asociándose a peor pronóstico y mayor riesgo de complicaciones.

questions.question: ¿Qué patrón de realce tardío de gadolinio es característico de miocarditis aguda?
questions.explanation: El realce tardío de gadolinio en la miocarditis aguda típicamente afecta la capa subepicárdica, a diferencia del patrón subendocárdico o transmural observado en infartos.

questions.question: What MRI sequence detects myocardial edema in myocarditis?
questions.explanation: The T2 STIR sequence is sensitive to myocardial edema, a key finding in acute myocarditis, while late enhancement is evaluated with T1 after gadolinium.

questions.question: Which Lake Louise criterion is considered positive for myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Los criterios de Lake Louise incluyen edema en T2 STIR, hiperemia en imágenes tempranas de T1 y realce tardío de gadolinio no isquémico, siendo el edema un criterio mayor.

questions.question: Which location of late enhancement suggests ischemic origin rather than myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Subendocardial or transmural enhancement follows the territory of a coronary artery and is typical of infarction, while subepicardial enhancement is more suggestive of myocarditis.

questions.question: ¿Qué hallazgo en resonancia magnética apoya el diagnóstico de miocarditis aguda?
questions.explanation: Subepicardial late enhancement is a characteristic and diagnostic finding in acute myocarditis, differentiating it from other patterns and supporting focal myocardial inflammation.

questions.question: ¿Qué capa cardíaca se afecta preferentemente en la miocarditis por realce tardío?
questions.explanation: La miocarditis afecta predominantemente el epicardio y el miocardio adyacente, manifestándose como realce tardío subepicárdico, a diferencia del compromiso endocárdico del infarto.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of fulminant myocarditis in young adults?
questions.explanation: Fulminant myocarditis in young adults is mainly caused by viral infections, such as parvovirus B19 and enterovirus, which cause acute myocardial damage and severe hemodynamic dysfunction.

questions.question: ¿Qué hallazgo hemodinámico caracteriza la miocarditis fulminante?
questions.explanation: La miocarditis fulminante se presenta con shock cardiogénico de rápida instauración, debido a la necrosis extensa del miocardio que compromete severamente la función de bomba, requiriendo soporte inotrópico o circulatorio.

questions.question: ¿Qué arritmia es causa frecuente de muerte súbita en la miocarditis aguda?
questions.explanation: La taquicardia ventricular, incluyendo la torsade de pointes, es la arritmia maligna más asociada a muerte súbita en pacientes con miocarditis aguda, debido a la inestabilidad eléctrica del miocardio inflamado.

questions.question: Which biomarker is typically elevated in acute myocarditis with myocardial damage?
questions.explanation: La troponina I de alta sensibilidad es el biomarcador más específico de daño miocárdico y se eleva en la miocarditis aguda, reflejando necrosis de los cardiomiocitos, aunque su elevación no es exclusiva de síndrome coronario.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es el tratamiento de primera línea en la miocarditis fulminante con shock?
questions.explanation: El soporte circulatorio mecánico, como balón de contrapulsación aórtica o ECMO, es el tratamiento inicial en la miocarditis fulminante con shock cardiogénico refractario, ya que permite mantener la perfusión mientras se recupera el miocardio.

questions.question: Which finding on cardiac MRI suggests acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Late gadolinium enhancement in a subepicardial or intramyocardial location is a characteristic finding of acute myocarditis on MRI, indicating necrosis or inflammatory fibrosis of the myocardium.

questions.question: What is the fundamental pillar of treatment in hemodynamically stable acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: In stable acute myocarditis, treatment is based on supportive measures such as rest, monitoring, and symptom management, since there is no specific therapy directed at viral inflammation.

questions.question: Why are NSAIDs contraindicated in acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: NSAIDs can exacerbate inflammatory damage and increase myocardial necrosis, worsening the prognosis, which is why they are contraindicated in the acute phase.

questions.question: What is the main indication for the use of glucocorticoids in acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Steroids are reserved for myocarditis of autoimmune cause, such as lupus or sarcoidosis, or in specific forms such as giant cell, not in typical viral myocarditis.

questions.question: In a patient with acute myocarditis and ventricular dysfunction, what drug is indicated as part of support?
questions.explanation: Los IECA están indicados en la disfunción ventricular izquierda para mejorar la función y el remodelado, siguiendo las guías de insuficiencia cardíaca en el contexto de miocarditis.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es el manejo inicial recomendado ante sospecha de miocarditis aguda sin signos de alarma?
questions.explanation: Physical rest and hospital observation are the basis of initial management, avoiding efforts that may increase the risk of arrhythmias or greater myocardial damage.

questions.question: What therapeutic alternative is correct in acute myocarditis due to viral causes?
questions.explanation: Viral myocarditis is managed with symptomatic support, as there is no evidence of benefit with steroids, colchicine, or immunoglobulin in the acute phase.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es la duración recomendada de restricción de ejercicio físico en miocarditis aguda?
questions.explanation: En miocarditis aguda, se recomienda restringir el ejercicio físico durante 3-6 meses para permitir la recuperación miocárdica y evitar arritmias o deterioro de la función ventricular.

questions.question: ¿Qué evaluación se debe realizar antes de permitir la reanudación del ejercicio en miocarditis?
questions.explanation: Previo al retorno al ejercicio, se recomienda una evaluación integral que incluya ecocardiograma para valorar función ventricular y prueba de esfuerzo para detectar arritmias o isquemia inducida.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es el principal riesgo de reanudar ejercicio intenso antes de los 3 meses en miocarditis aguda?
questions.explanation: El ejercicio intenso precoz en miocarditis aguda puede desencadenar arritmias ventriculares malignas y muerte súbita, debido a la inflamación y vulnerabilidad eléctrica del miocardio.

questions.question: What type of exercise is allowed during the first 3 months in acute myocarditis?
questions.explanation: Durante los primeros 3 meses, solo se permite ejercicio aeróbico de bajo impacto (caminar, trotar suave) bajo supervisión, evitando esfuerzos intensos que aumenten el riesgo de complicaciones.

questions.question: ¿Qué hallazgo en la resonancia magnética cardíaca contraindica el reinicio de ejercicio a los 3 meses?
questions.explanation: La presencia de edema miocárdico persistente en la resonancia magnética indica inflamación activa, por lo que se debe prolongar la restricción de ejercicio hasta su resolución.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es el objetivo principal de la restricción de ejercicio físico de 3-6 meses en miocarditis?
options: Evitar la aparición de hipertrofia ventricular
Prevenir la progresión a insuficiencia cardíaca
Reduce the risk of sudden death
questions.explanation: La restricción de ejercicio busca evitar el estrés hemodinámico sobre el miocardio inflamado, reduciendo así el riesgo de arritmias mortales y muerte súbita durante la fase aguda.
